title: Attention kernel cost-gating and staged compatibility rollout for v2/v3
creator: Priya Gupta
description:
Goal: Introduce a cost-aware gating layer in the runtime that chooses between FlashAttention v2 and v3 (and compatible hybrid kernels) using a lightweight per-request cost model, and roll it out gradually with strong telemetry-driven rollback safeguards.

Why: v3 provides latency improvements on many workloads but shows memory pressure and p95 degradations on long-context patterns and certain micro-batched traffic shapes. Ops teams report sporadic regressions after naive v3 rollouts. A cost-gate lets us optimize for unit-cost and latency while preventing customer-impacting regressions.

Scope: implement runtime decision function, offline tuning harness to build cost/compatibility tables by model family + sequence-length profile + GPU type (A100/H100/V100), add CI checks and a feature-flagged canary rollout with automated rollback triggers.

Non-goals: global autoscaling changes and model re-compilation. This ticket only touches kernel selection, gating policy, telemetry, and rollout automation.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a per-request kernel_decision hook that evaluates a cost_score and compatibility_flag before dispatching to a kernel variant.
Cost model populated with benchmark table for at least two model families (decoder-only Llama-like, encoder-decoder) and sequences lengths [16, 128, 512, 2048, 8192] on A100/H100.
Integration tests that simulate microbatch shapes and long-context prompts demonstrating chosen kernel is consistent with policy for >99% of synthetic traces.
Canary rollout automation that can shift traffic 0->1->5->20% with telemetry checks and automatic rollback on predefined SLAs.
Documentation (Confluence) describing gating heuristics, how to add new kernel variants, and operational runbook for rollbacks.
comments: 2026-03-01 Priya Gupta: Created ticket. Collected initial customer incident notes from SRE; linked to parent runtime fingerprinting epic ENG-305678.

2026-03-03 Diego Morales: Ran quick microbenchmarks on A100: for seq=512, v3 p50=22ms vs v2 p50=28ms; for seq=8192 v3 p95 spikes and p95>v2 by ~18% due to workspace fragmentation. Logged traces to telemetry dashboard.
2026-03-06 Ava Chen (Perf): Proposed a cost_score = alpha*latency_est + beta*mem_headroom_penalty + gamma*quant_degradation where weights tuned per model family. Draft cost table uploaded to Drive.
2026-03-08 Diego Morales: Prototype hook implemented in runtime branch feat/attn-cost-gate. Simple decision: if mem_headroom < 12% prefer v2. Running CI microbench suite now.

2026-03-10 QA: Found a regression when interleaving short-chat and long-context traces; gate toggled per-request did a kernel switch causing KV cache thrash. Added a sticky-decision window (10s) to avoid oscillation.
2026-03-12 Design Review with PM (Liam O'Connor): Agreed to expose per-route override in Console and restrict auto-upgrade to non-production API keys unless explicitly allowed.
2026-03-14 Diego Morales: Canary config ready. Added automated rollback rules: >5% increase in p95 or >10% increase in error-rate over canary baseline triggers immediate rollback and alert to oncall.
2026-03-14 Priya Gupta: Marking next steps: finalize benchmark matrix for H100, add kernel warmup amortization metric, and submit PR for review.
telemetry_summary: Key signals: p50_latency, p95_latency, tokens_per_sec, allocation_failure_rate, memory_headroom_percent, kernel_switch_rate. Baseline computed from last 7 days of traffic. Canary thresholds: p95 <= baseline*1.05; error_rate <= baseline + 0.5pp; kernel_switch_rate < 0.2/s per instance. We also track cost_per_1M_tokens estimated from GPU time and token throughput.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal synthetic canary on Q/A cluster with model-families A/B (0%). Phase 1: 1% traffic on non-prod API keys (24h). Phase 2: 5% mixed traffic across regions (48h). Phase 3: 20% for 72h with extended telemetry. Phase 4: full rollout gated by release manager signoff. Each phase has automated checks; failure triggers immediate rollback. Operators can pin route to v2/v3 via Console. Sticky-decision window (10s) avoids oscillation across requests from same connection.
